## PDF page 76

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=76)

```text
                               CHAPTER FIVE



                            BLOCKERS


Blockers and combos go hand-in-hand. A blocker is simply a visible card
that reduces the combinations of a specific hand. Since there is only one of
each rank+suit in the deck, by holding a specific card you make it impossible
for your opponents to hold hands that use that specific card.

So if you hold the A♠, it is impossible for your opponent to hold A♠K♠.

If the flop is J♥T♦6♥, the J♥ and T♦ being visible block two possible JTs combos.

Blockers are super important preflop as they can reduce the combos of
monster starting hands. When you hold certain hands, say A5s, you reduce
the possibility of your opponent holding combos of AA and AK. Note that your
A5s does not eliminate ALL possibilities of AA and AK, but minimizing some
combinations of strong starting hands can be helpful when finding extra
aggression preflop.

When it comes to blockers, there are two rules to remember:

   1. With pocket pairs, use the 6, 3, 1, 0 rule. This means there are 6 combos
     with zero blockers, 3 combos if there is a single blocker, 1 combo if
     there are two blockers, and 0 combos if there are three blockers.
     So if you hold 77, you block zero combinations of KK, and thus your
     opponent can have all six combos of KK. If you hold 87s, they can only


                                    PA G E 7 6
```

## PDF page 77

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=77)

```text
                             BLOCKERS: SIMPLIFIED


     have three combos of 88. If you hold AA, there is only one possible
     combo of AA left.

   2. With unpaired starting hands, multiply together the number of unseen
     cards. Normally there are 16 combos of all AK (4 unseen Aces * 4
     unseen Kings), but if you have ATo, you reduce their AK combos down
     to 12 (3 unseen Aces * 4 unseen Kings). If you have A♥J♣, they can only
     have 3 combos of JTs (since the J♣T♣ combo is now impossible).

There are tons of high-value spots to work blockers into your postflop tech-
nical skillset, but this section is going to focus on blocker usage preflop.

TOOLS TO USE: Flopzilla or Equilab if need be. Seasoned players should be
able to do this first section off the top of their heads.

PROCESS: Quickly jot down how many combos of these five common hand
types exist after taking your own hole cards into consideration. Keep in mind
that AK includes both suited and unsuited versions, while QJs and 87s only
include the suited versions. If you are going to use Flopzilla, plug your starting
hand into the dead cards first.




TAKEAWAYS: Notice how your Ace-high hands block combos of their
strongest starting hands (AA and AK) compared to other starting hands.

GLGL.


                                     PA G E 7 7
```
